EEPROMDeviceFirmware

Renaming "EEPROM" to "EEPROMDeviceFirmware" creates a naming style inconsistency with other components like BIOS or XDPE1X2XX, which are already defined in the same firmware.json in other active commits. Given this inconsistency, should we still proceed with renaming it to "EEPROMDeviceFirmware"?

BIOS is a special case as that by itself is firmware so it doesn't necessitate that suffix (will seem redundant), but other devices should have that as schema is for firmware info. I have already requested this for VR one.
Done
Here better to list the eeprom based devices, such as RetimerFirmware

The string "EEPROM" applies to all EEPROM-based devices, not just retimers or FRUs. It exports a xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROM interface for the EEPROM device code updater daemon. How about changing it to EEPROMDevice to export xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMDevice? Listing "RetimerFirmware" in Type may mislead users into thinking it's limited to specific components.

> The string "EEPROM" applies to all EEPROM-based devices, not just retimers or FRUs. It exports a xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROM interface for the EEPROM device code updater daemon. 

The EEPROM device updater can register to handle EM config update for all eeprom based devices. So, it will watch for, e.g. - xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMRetimerFirmware, xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMXXXFirmware, etc.

But i am fine if you want to keep it generic and name enum for Type as "EEPROMDeviceFirmware". We can revisit this later if someone thinks otherwise.
Done
MuxGPIOs
Done.

Done

I don't think the current EEPROM definition supports this today?  Can we get this split into two commits.

1 commit for the existing functionality that we're (correctly) making enforced in json schema
2nd commit for the new functions you're adding?

It's not clear to me why a fru eeprom would have an iana and device compatibility descriptor, but having it separate will get a commit message that describes why its needed, so that should help.

You can refer to https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YdO_EXCRO9UQnmot6nbGWw88QTXv76-lbiKNrVPjaSI/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.46v7asziecay and https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/74653.
The IANA and device compatibility descriptor are utilized in the new code updaters for image validation.

First one looks to be a private google doc that isn't public and isn't related to openbmc, so not really sure what to do with that.

I'm not really sure how https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/74653 got approved, given that IANA isn't really a property of an eeprom or of a piece of hardware and violates some of the design of entity-manager in that it adds openbmc-specific and company specific software identifiers to a hardware specific file.  I'm not sure how that would work in practice unless you assume that each company never shares the same hardware.

I'll read more.  Maybe there's something in the design that deals with that?

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/74653

shows adding it to a CPLD, where it might make sense (a given CPLD is made by a known manufacturer)

This is adding it to an eeprom device.  I suspect this has made some missteps on what the above doc intended.

> https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/74653
> 
> shows adding it to a CPLD, where it might make sense (a given CPLD is made by a known manufacturer)
> 
> This is adding it to an eeprom device.  I suspect this has made some missteps on what the above doc intended.

Here EEPROM is not the FRU EEPROM but its the EERPOM for a device such as Retimer (for example, https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/hwmon/pt5161l.c#L666) whose Firmware Image resides on that.

@ed@tanous.net The intent here is to manage firmware updates for EEPROM-based devices, such as Retimers, in a manner similar to CPLD firmware updates. Let me know if you have any further concerns. Thanks!
Right, we already have an EEPROM type.  Does this differ in the actual hardware interfaces?  Or just how software treats it (reads through fru device instead of firmware update daemon).

It's a difference in how the software handles it. For example, with a Retimer, the firmware update daemon reads the firmware version from the Retimer itself but writes the firmware image to the external EEPROM connected to it.

> It's a difference in how the software handles it.

Great, so if the hardware is the same, reuse the existing hardware type, and add the appropriate properties to it to denote that it's used for firmware.

> For example, with a Retimer, the firmware update daemon reads the firmware version from the Retimer itself but writes the firmware image to the external EEPROM connected to it.

Yep, this is what I suspected.  New "type" isn't required here, just one new property to denote that an at24 is used for "firmware" versus "fru".

@ed@tanous.net So, in case there are multiple devices of this type how would one relate which eeprom is for which device, for example, EEPROM24at04X (Device EEPROM) and EEPROMpt5161l (Actual Device) as they will be two separate expose entries then.
Is there some way to create a relation here or one is expected to use the same name label to create these relations?
Hi @ed@tanous.net Do you have any suggestions on how to create a relationship between EEPROMpt5161l and EEPROM24at04X?
Done

Since you have defined MuxGPIOs as an array of nested object, i suppose this will show on DBus as indexed interfaces, for example,

xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMDeviceFirmware.MuxGPIOs0
xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMDeviceFirmware.MuxGPIOs1
...
xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMDeviceFirmware.MuxGPIOsX

Have you verified this by providing a test configuration? This will make the reactor side handling more involved and we won't be able to use the phosphor-dbus-interfaces generated bindings.

Yes, it will show on DBus as indexed xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMDeviceFirmware.MuxGPIOsX. Since there are cases where multiple GPIOs need to be set up to mux the EEPROM device to the BMC, this approach ensures flexibility in handling different hardware configurations.

I understand that this makes the reactor-side handling more involved and prevents the use of phosphor-dbus-interfaces generated bindings. Do you have any suggestions or alternative ways to structure this on DBus while still supporting multiple GPIOs for muxing?

> Yes, it will show on DBus as indexed xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.EEPROMDeviceFirmware.MuxGPIOsX. Since there are cases where multiple GPIOs need to be set up to mux the EEPROM device to the BMC, this approach ensures flexibility in handling different hardware configurations.
> 
> I understand that this makes the reactor-side handling more involved and prevents the use of phosphor-dbus-interfaces generated bindings. Do you have any suggestions or alternative ways to structure this on DBus while still supporting multiple GPIOs for muxing?


One way you can handle this is to specify array of individual properties rather than array of nested objects. You can refer to BIOS schema here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/75948/25/schemas/firmware.json.

Why is this a separate schema? Is there any intent to share it?

Otherwise can probably inline those properties to simplify.

This schema is defined separately to enable reuse of common configuration properties that are based on a combination of bus, address, and chip model. For example, both `DeviceInfo` and `EEPROMInfo` use this structure to describe how to access devices over I2C. By referencing a shared schema, we avoid duplication and ensure consistency across components that interact with similar hardware.
Ok, looks like i missed that. Thanks for clarify 😊
Since it's specifically aimed at i2c devices, can we rename it to ```I2CDeviceProperties``` or similar?
Done

Removed `DevicePropertiesDef` and inlined its properties into each schema to allow ChipModel enumeration and improve clarity. Reused existing Bus and Address types from legacy.json to avoid confusion.
Is "ChipModel" an enum? Which values will be supported here.
Yes, but I intentionally avoid restricting the supported values in this common schema since this property is shared across multiple schemas.

Yes, but there needs to be a way for people to see which values will be supported here. There will be values which the daemon does not handle and that can already be expressed in the configuration schema.

If there is no way to enumerate, maybe 2 "ChipModel" properties can be part of the "EEPROMDeviceFirmware" schema? Then they can be enumerated there since they are no longer shared.

>  I intentionally avoid restricting the supported values

The intent of EM is to have a listing of what things are supported.  Please make this an enum.

ALso, if these types are things like AT04 devices that we already support, please roll your definitions into those types.
Moved the `ChipModel` into the `EEPROMDeviceFirmware` schema.
ChipModel should not exist.  Follow the model of the EEPROM24at04X that already exists.
Done

probably needs the 

additionalProperties: false

stanza
Why do we need "additionalProperties: false"?

Since we do not want configurations to pass the validator if they use properties not listed in their schema.

https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core#section-10.3.2.3


There is an active patch to fix this for an IBM schema https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/79654

and now the (reviewers) need to figure out if these additional Properties in these configurations are actually supported, if the schema has to be changed, or the configurations.

So better to avoid these problems by using 

```
"additionalProperties": false
```

EEPROMDeviceFirmware 

would instead be

EEPROMAT04256, which is a type we already support.  I suspect we just need to add something to the existing type that indicates the "expected contents"

Understood. Added "additionalProperties: false".

@ed@tanous.net EEPROMDeviceFirmware is for devices that use a separate EEPROM to store their firmware but read the firmware version directly from the device itself, such as a Retimer.
Can you add to this description which daemon will initially consume this configuration.

Please don't add the daemon name in the schema description.  Add it into the commit message.

At a schema level, it shouldn't matter what daemon consumes a config stanza.

> At a schema level, it shouldn't matter what daemon consumes a config stanza.

Yes. But how do you then find that daemon without building an image and monitoring dbus at runtime?
